create.title: Inverse-selector reciprocity and scalar projective-capacity obstruction
create.statement_tex: Fix the flat-smooth strict-UNBAL M2 owner with X=N_0+xi, D=X^delta, L=X^ell, R=X/D, K=XL/D^2, Delta=D/L, 1/4<=delta<1/2, 0<=ell<delta-1/4, 178ell+1638delta>463, and a=delta-ell. For every coprime j,n, arbitrary inverse representatives, every integer h, and either parity of j, e(-h inverse(j mod n)/n)=e(h inverse(n mod j)/j-h/(jn)). In the centered owner this gives the literal 1/(gnj) summand with chi_4(g)chi_4(n), real centre, moving support, profiles, endpoints, arbitrary gcd strata, and all 1<=h<n retained. Complete h modulo n summation reconstructs the original reciprocal row exactly, and only the accepted h=0 modulo n Ramanujan row is removed once. For every A subset of (Z/jZ)^x, M=|A|, the unweighted kernel F_(j,A)(u,h)=e(h inverse(u mod j)/j), 1<=h<=j-1, satisfies F F*=jI_M-11*, with singular values sqrt(j) of multiplicity M-1 and sqrt(j-M) once. Hence every exact Hilbert rank-one scalarization followed termwise by triangle pays at least the nuclear norm, and for A=(Z/jZ)^x its nuclear-to-Hilbert--Schmidt inflation is asymptotic to sqrt(phi(j))=j^(1/2-o(1)). The normalized positive block 1<=h<=j has orthonormal rows. The full physical range has exact residue-compression norm sqrt(ceil((n-1)/j)) asymptotic to sqrt(Delta); positive h=mj survive with inverse phase one. At g=1, j asymptotic to K, both K^(1/2-o(1)) and X^(a/2) exceed the missing boundary factor X^mu(a) at each fixed strict exponent pair, where mu(a)=a-1/4 for a<=1/3 and mu(a)=(1-2a)/4 for a>=1/3. The exact additive common-test expansion is a full-rank change of basis with high additive bandwidth. The audited scalar Bettin--Chandee/Wright, Blomer--Milicevic, Deshouillers--Iwaniec, Assing--Blomer--Li, and level-four/eight realizations do not absorb the joint coefficient, projective cost, long complement, moving support, high bandwidth, and growing levels at an owner-saving norm. This is only a no-go for exact unweighted Hilbert scalarization plus termwise triangle and the named audited scalar routes. It is not a lower bound for the signed scalar or literal weighted matrix, does not exclude an additional compensating scalar saving, and does not exclude a bespoke vector theorem acting on the complete weighted matrix before positive norms. No target, strict range, downstream owner, or exponent is proved.

reject.reason: Reciprocity is an exact identity. Its inverse-residue kernel has full finite rank, and complete frequency summation reconstructs the original reciprocal row.
The frozen hypotheses contain no nonzero lower buffer with complete unit-class coverage, and diagonal or entrywise weights can reduce nuclear mass.
Support, regularity, zero extension, and upper bounds do not imply a quantitative interval on which the joint profile is bounded below.
The centered deletion removes h=0 modulo n. Positive h=mj are zero only modulo j and remain in 1<=h<n.
The nuclear norm is a lower price for exact Hilbert rank-one factorization closed termwise by triangle, not a lower bound for the signed owner.
The high-frequency mass is an exact finite diagnostic. A spectral Sobolev or Bessel loss requires a theorem-specific match to printed hypotheses.
Mellin encoding with arithmetic period lcm(4,j) creates growing levels; for prime j=p the audited family includes levels through 4p^2 and 8p^2.
The sourced band covers only a proportion asymptotic to 1/(Dg) of the physical row, and no theorem controls the complement for free.
Complete h orthogonality is a hostile control that returns the original reciprocal row exactly after the already safe zero row is accounted for.
The audit excludes only named scalar interfaces at owner-saving cost. A new coefficient-sensitive vector theorem remains logically open.
The no-go scopes a proposed scalar continuation. It proves neither the positive owner estimate nor any strict target-safe range.
No M2 parent, M9, or bridge is closed, so neither the internal nor external global exponent changes.
The nuclear lower price applies to exact rank-one scalarization followed termwise by triangle. It does not constrain a theorem that acts on the joint matrix before positive norms.
The long-block norm and self-return are capacity identities, not lower bounds for the Kloosterman-weighted signed complement.
Inversion permutes every unit class for even and odd j, and the exact Gram identity remains valid without a parity restriction.
